Oppelt et al. [@oppelt2018model] also measured the TNFα response under drugs causing liver
injury: diclofenac (DCF) with the imaging and blots of the first chapters, and amiodarone (AMD),
paracetamol (APAP), fialuridine (FIAU) and ximelagatran (XIM) with four blots. Which pathway
processes does each compound change? The publication answered this for DCF with an L1 penalty on
the differences of all rate constants between treated and untreated cells, scanned over the
penalty strength. Here all five compounds are the groups of a spike-and-slab random effect: a
compound leaves a rate constant unchanged or changes it by a normal draw, with probability and
spread of changes estimated from all compounds together. Code: `compounds.R`, on the reduced model
of [Profile likelihood](guide-profiles.html); random effects and `em()` are introduced in
[Nonlinear mixed-effects models](guide-nlme.html).

The second part lists the sparse random-effect distributions (spike-and-slab, Dirichlet-process)
and what their fits report; derivations are in [Methods > Sparsity priors](methods-sparsity-priors.html).

## Compound data

Each compound has a separate control: DCF on the blots and imaging of the first chapters, the other
four on a third blot set with their own untreated, stimulated control. A condition without compound
belongs to no group (`NA` in column `compound`).

```{r compounddata}
```

```{r}
covariates(dataCompounds)
```

## Spike-and-slab random effects

With $\theta_k$ the log rate constant $k$ and $\eta_{ik}$ the change by compound $i$, a condition
with compound $i$ uses $\theta_k + \eta_{ik}$, one without uses $\theta_k$. The spike-and-slab
distribution [@mitchell1988bayesian; @george1993variable] of a change is

$$p(\eta_{ik}) = (1 - \rho)\, \delta(\eta_{ik}) + \rho\, \mathcal{N}(\eta_{ik};\, 0, \tau^2),$$

a spike at 0 with weight $1 - \rho$ and a normal slab of standard deviation $\tau$ with weight
$\rho$. Changes are independent across compounds and rate constants; $\rho$, $\tau$ are shared.
`em()` estimates $\theta$, $\rho$ and $\tau$ from the likelihood with the changes integrated out, a
sum over the subsets of changed rate constants
([Methods > Sparsity priors](methods-sparsity-priors.html#approximate-marginal)). The
posterior spike probability $p_0 = \Pr(\eta_{ik} = 0 \mid y)$ near 0 means a change, near the prior
$1 - \rho$ no evidence, above it evidence against a change.

```{r, include = FALSE}
fit <- stored("results/compounds.rds", "compounds.R", envir = new.env())
rateConstants <- length(unique(fit$random$eta))
```

Each compound has `r rateConstants` candidate rate constants, and the subset sum is exact; beyond
a term budget `em()` uses the expectation consistent (EC) approximation
([Methods > Spike and slab](methods-sparsity-priors.html#spike-and-slab)). Comparison with the
L1 penalty: [Methods > Selection of deviations](methods-sparsity-priors.html#selection-of-deviations).

`x ~ 1 + (1 | gr(compound, dist = spikeSlab()))` in `insert()` replaces rate constant `x` by a
fixed effect plus a compound random effect. Candidates are the rate constants the reduced model
estimates, all but gauge and fixed values of the publication. Scales and offsets of the third blot
set are separate parameters, except `off_IkBa`, fixed at 0 by the reduced model.

## Joint fit of all compounds

`em()` estimates fixed effects, change modes, $\rho$ and $\tau$ together. `compounds.R` runs 200
starts, the reduced optimum with changes at 0 and 199 around it, redrawing failed starts; `helix.R`
splits them into `distributedComputing()` tasks by `msem(which = )`
([Remote computing](guide-remote-computing.html)):

```{r compoundfit, eval = FALSE}
```

The best fit is saved with a table of all starts:

```{r compoundsave, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r}
fit <- readRDS("results/compounds.rds")
c(value = fit$value, converged = fit$converged, iterations = fit$iterations)
fit$argument[c("prob_compound", "tau_compound")]
fit$coupling
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
couplingText <- switch(fit$coupling %||% "none",
  expectationConsistent = "the expectation consistent (EC) approximation",
  none = "none: every compound is integrated exactly")
```

`value` is $-2 \log L$ of the approximate marginal, `iterations` the steps of the joint trust
region of fixed effects and hyperparameters, `coupling` the integral over coupled changes, here
`r couplingText`.

## Multistart optimization

The objective has local optima. `msem()` redraws a start whose fit fails, e.g. where EC does not
converge. `$multistart` has per start `value`, `converged`, `iterations`, attempts (`tries`) and the
`error` of a start that failed every attempt. The waterfall shows the best 100 starts; a plateau is
one optimum.

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
plotValues(fit, rank(value, ties.method = "first") <= 100)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
ms <- fit$multistart
best <- min(ms$value, na.rm = TRUE)
multistartText <- sprintf(
  "Of the %d starts, %d end within 1 of the best -2 log L, %d did not converge and %d failed.",
  nrow(ms), sum(ms$value < best + 1, na.rm = TRUE), sum(!ms$converged & !is.na(ms$value)),
  sum(is.na(ms$value)))
retriedText <- if (is.null(ms$tries) || !any(ms$tries > 1)) "" else
  sprintf("%d of the starts were drawn again, %d times in all.", sum(ms$tries > 1), sum(ms$tries - 1))
```

`r multistartText` `r retriedText`

## Changes by compound

Changes with $p_0 < 0.05$, with log-scale modes:

```{r}
changes <- fit$random[fit$random$p0 < 0.05, c("group", "eta", "mode", "se", "p0")]
changes <- changes[order(changes$group, changes$p0), ]
rownames(changes) <- NULL
changes
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
compounds <- sort(unique(fit$random$group))
rates <- unique(fit$random$eta)
counts <- table(factor(changes$group, levels = compounds))
others <- setdiff(compounds, "DCF")
changesText <- sprintf(
  "DCF changes %d of the %d rate constants, %s. The probability of a change is %.2f, and a change has a spread of %.2f on the log scale, a factor of about %.1f.",
  counts[["DCF"]], length(rates), enumerate(sprintf("%s %d", others, counts[others])),
  fit$argument[["prob_compound"]], fit$argument[["tau_compound"]], exp(fit$argument[["tau_compound"]]))
# the seven rate constants the L1 scan of the publication selected for DCF, by reaction
publication <- c(act_Ikk_by_TNF = "IKK activation by TNFα", trigger_iIkk = "IKK recovery",
                 act_pIkk = "IKK phosphorylation", act_Ikb_by_Ikk = "IκBα phosphorylation by pIKK",
                 prod_mIkb_by_nNfk = "IκBα transcription", degrad_mIkb = "IκBα transcript degradation",
                 build_A20 = "A20 translation")
reactions <- c(publication, shuttle_RnaA20 = "the delay of the A20 transcript")
named <- function(x) ifelse(x %in% names(reactions), paste0(reactions[x], " (`", x, "`)"), paste0("`", x, "`"))
dcf <- changes$eta[changes$group == "DCF"]
shared <- intersect(names(publication), dcf)
publicationText <- paste0(
  sprintf("Of the %d rate constants the L1 scan of the publication selected for DCF, the spike and slab finds %d: %s",
          length(publication), length(shared), enumerate(named(shared))),
  if (length(setdiff(names(publication), dcf)))
    sprintf("; not %s", enumerate(named(setdiff(names(publication), dcf)))),
  if (length(setdiff(dcf, names(publication))))
    sprintf(", but %s", enumerate(named(setdiff(dcf, names(publication))))),
  ".")
```

`r changesText` `r publicationText` [@oppelt2018model]

```{r, fig.height = 5.5}
shown <- fit$random
shown$eta <- factor(shown$eta, levels = unique(shown$eta))
shown$evidence <- -log10(pmax(shown$p0, 1e-6))
ggplot2::ggplot(shown, ggplot2::aes(group, eta)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(ggplot2::aes(fill = mode, alpha = evidence), color = "white") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = shown[shown$p0 < 0.05, ], ggplot2::aes(shape = "p0 < 0.05"),
                      fill = "white") +
  ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b") +
  ggplot2::scale_alpha(range = c(0.1, 1), limits = c(0, 6), breaks = 1:3,
                       labels = c("1, p0 = 0.1", "2, p0 = 0.01", "3, p0 = 0.001"),
                       guide = ggplot2::guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = "gray30"))) +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = 21) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "change [log]", alpha = "evidence, -log10 p0", shape = NULL) +
  theme_dMod()
```

Each tile is one $\eta_{ik}$; rate constants follow the pathway from IKK (top) to A20 (bottom).
Color is the log-scale mode of the most probable structure: red increase, blue decrease, white no
change (wherever the spike is more probable than the slab); $-0.7$ halves a rate constant. Opacity
is the evidence $-\log_{10} p_0$, full from 6 on ($p_0 < 10^{-6}$). A pale tile is a small change,
or $p_0$ near or above $1 - \rho$; circles mark $p_0 < 0.05$, the table above. A colored tile without
circle has $p_0$ between 0.05 and 0.5.

## Data and fit by compound

Prediction per compound at the estimated fixed effects and changes against the compound data, each
point with the measured standard deviation, which the blots have in place of an error model; gray:
the untreated, stimulated control of the same blots at the fixed effects alone. DCF blots span six
hours, the others 50 minutes:

::: {.wide}
```{r, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 8.5}
outer <- getParameters(prdCompounds)
estimates <- c(fit$argument, fit$fixed, setNames(fit$random$mode, fit$random$parameter))
pars <- setNames(numeric(length(outer)), outer)
pars[intersect(outer, names(estimates))] <- estimates[intersect(outer, names(estimates))]

treated <- grep("^TNF_[A-Z]", names(dataCompounds), value = TRUE)
controls <- sub("^TNF_[A-Z]+_", "TNF_none_", treated)
observed <- as.data.frame(dataCompounds)
times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 60, length.out = 200), seq(0, max(observed$time), length.out = 200))))
prediction <- as.data.frame(prdCompounds(times, pars, deriv = FALSE, conditions = union(treated, controls)))

# every compound with the untreated control on the same blots
blots <- c("IkBa", "pIkBa", "pIKK", "pNFkB")
byCompound <- function(frame) do.call(rbind, Map(function(cond, ctl) {
  rows <- frame[frame$condition %in% c(cond, ctl) & frame$name %in% blots,
                c("time", "name", "value", "sigma", "condition")]
  rows$compound <- sub("^TNF_([A-Z]+)_.*", "\\1", cond)
  rows$treatment <- ifelse(rows$condition == cond, "compound", "control")
  rows
}, treated, controls))
points <- byCompound(observed)
# the curves over the time range of the data of the compound
curves <- byCompound(prediction)
curves <- curves[curves$time <= tapply(points$time, points$compound, max)[curves$compound], ]
colors <- c(compound = "#b2182b", control = "gray55")
ggplot2::ggplot(mapping = ggplot2::aes(time, value, color = treatment)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = curves) +
  ggplot2::geom_errorbar(data = points, ggplot2::aes(ymin = value - sigma, ymax = value + sigma),
                         width = 0) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = points) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(name ~ compound, scales = "free") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 3)) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "time [min]", y = "log signal [a.u.]", color = NULL) +
  theme_dMod() +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
:::

## Sparse random-effect distributions

`gr(group, dist = )` sets the random-effect distribution of a term. Besides `normal()`, two have
deviations exactly zero unless the data need them:

| distribution | a deviation $\eta$ of a group | hyperparameters |
|---|---|---|
| `spikeSlab()` | $0$ with probability $1 - \rho$, else $\mathcal{N}(0, \tau^2)$ | `prob_<grouping>`, `tau_<grouping>` |
| `dirichletProcess()` | cluster value: $0$ for the population cluster, else one $\mathcal{N}(0, \tau^2)$ draw | `concentration_<grouping>`, `tau_<grouping>` |

Hyperparameters are shared by the symbols of a term, numbered `_1`, `_2`, ... for several terms
of one grouping, and estimated with the fixed effects unless given, as in `spikeSlab(tau = 0.5)`.
A spike-and-slab deviation is zero with a probability reported per group. Under the Dirichlet process groups share deviations in clusters with the population
value, see [Dirichlet-process random effects](#dirichlet-process-random-effects). Normal and sparse
random effects of one grouping combine; `em(method = "focei")` fits all, Dirichlet-process ones
also `method = "saem"`.

## Fitting sparse random effects

`em(method = "focei")` integrates sparse random effects on the Laplace approximation of the data
term at the joint mode of a group, exactly where possible, the spike-and-slab effects of a group
jointly even where the data couple them, and by EC where the data link a Dirichlet-process effect
to another factor or the subset sum leaves the budget. Fixed
effects and hyperparameters move in one trust region: no EM iteration count, no random numbers.
`fit$coupling` is `"expectationConsistent"` if a group needed EC, `NULL` if all are exact. Integral,
gradient and hyperparameter steps:
[Methods > Approximate marginal](methods-sparsity-priors.html#approximate-marginal),
[Methods > Expectation consistent
approximation](methods-sparsity-priors.html#expectation-consistent-approximation) and
[Methods > Joint trust region](methods-sparsity-priors.html#joint-trust-region).

| entry of `control$sparseFit` | default | controls |
|---|---|---|
| `maxOuter` | `200` | joint trust-region iterations, all runs |
| `trustControl` | `rinit = 1`, `rmax = 10`, `ftol = 1e-10`, `mtol = 1e-5` | joint trust region, as `trust()` |

Other entries are an error. The compound fit passes the `tolerances` of
[Setting up models](guide-model.html) in `trustControl`, above the solver error in value and gradient. A run stopping
short of `mtol` restarts while runs lower $-2 \log L$ by more than `mtol`. `msem()` perturbs
concentrations and slab standard deviations on log scale, slab probabilities on logit scale.

## Reported structure

The fit reports the most probable structure: subset of deviations (spike and slab) or partition
(Dirichlet process). Spike deviations are exactly zero, slab deviations the posterior mean given
the structure ([Methods > Reported structure](methods-sparsity-priors.html#reported-structure)).
`fit$random` has a row per group and random effect:

- `mode`, this value;
- `se`, posterior standard deviation over spike and slab;
- spike-and-slab and Dirichlet process: `cluster`, 0 for the population value, 1, 2, ... for
  deviating groups or clusters in group order, and `p0`, posterior probability of zero deviation;
- `data`, whether the random effect reaches data of the group, where some do not.

A sparse random effect reaching no data of the group (through transformations, ODE, observables,
error model) rests at 0 with the prior standard deviation and, for spike and slab,
$p_0 = 1 - \rho$. `fit$slab` lists probabilities, concentrations and slab standard deviations,
each with term symbols, estimate and whether fixed.

## Standard errors

With spike-and-slab random effects `fit$hessian` is `NULL`; `vcov()` inverts
`fit$information`, the empirical information from the group scores. It needs more groups than
parameters, or conditions without random effects plus priors for the other directions; otherwise
`vcov()` is an error and standard errors are `NA`. In the compound fit the conditions without
compound and the prior complete the five compounds. `dirichletProcess()` fits have neither;
`confint(method = "profile")` gives intervals. Details: [Methods > Standard errors](methods-sparsity-priors.html#standard-errors).

## Dirichlet-process random effects

With `gr(group, dist = dirichletProcess())` groups and population value form clusters; the
concentration $\alpha$ sets how readily a group opens a new one. The population cluster has
deviation zero, every other cluster one common deviation from $\mathcal{N}(0, \tau^2)$. $\alpha$ and
$\tau$ are estimated by marginal maximum likelihood in one fit, with no penalty to scan. The
reported structure is that of spike and slab with clusters in place of single deviations; the
compounds here are fitted without it.

`method = "focei"` sums exactly over partitions of up to 14 groups. `method = "saem"` draws
partitions, allowing normal random effects alongside but no other sparse ones, and reports the most
frequent partition of the late draws, from `window` iterations after burn-in, with standard error
`valueSE` of $-2 \log L$.
`control$saem$particles` sets the importance-sampling particles, default 500; `converged` says
whether burn-in ended by the drift test. An SAEM fit has no gradient, Hessian or empirical
information. Details:
[Methods > Sparsity priors](methods-sparsity-priors.html#dirichlet-process-random-effects).

Reference: `randomEffects()`, `spikeSlab()`, `dirichletProcess()`, `em()`, `msem()`,
`plotValues()`
